candidates.title: [Reference guide for the clinical management of adult Langerhans cell histiocytosis (key points from the first edition, 2025)].
candidates.abstract: According to the registry of the Japanese Society of Hematology, adult histiocytic neoplasms are extremely rare, with approximately 40 cases reported annually, and the most common among them is Langerhans cell histiocytosis (LCH). Lesions may involve multiple organs, including bone, skin, lung, the central nervous system, and the endocrine system. Without a hematology perspective, the neoplastic nature of LCH may not be apparent, resulting in missed diagnoses. Central diabetes insipidus, anterior pituitary dysfunction, and LCH-associated neurodegeneration, once developed, often result in irreversible impairment. Because delayed therapeutic intervention can result in permanent organ damage, it is essential for hematologists to understand the "minimum initial management" required to protect patient outcomes. This review summarizes the key points of diagnosis and initial management in adult LCH based on the first edition of the Adult LCH Clinical Reference Guide (2025).
candidates.journal: [Rinsho ketsueki] The Japanese journal of clinical hematology

candidates.title: Pregnancy in Autoimmune Polyglandular Syndrome Type 3c With Graves' Disease and Myasthenia Gravis: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Autoimmune polyglandular syndrome type 3c (APS3c), characterized by autoimmune thyroid disease with another organ-specific autoimmune disorder in the absence of adrenal insufficiency, is an uncommon presentation. Its coexistence with Graves' disease and myasthenia gravis (MG) is rare and poses additional diagnostic and therapeutic challenges, particularly when complicated by thyroid storm and pregnancy. We report the ongoing management of a 22-year-old woman with this combination of autoimmune disorders. She was admitted with thyroid storm diagnosed using the Burch-Wartofsky Point Scale and Japan Thyroid Association criteria after a 15-month history of weight loss, heat intolerance, diaphoresis, anxiety, palpitations, unilateral ptosis, and fatigable proximal upper-extremity weakness. Graves' disease and MG were diagnosed based on clinical findings, positive thyroid-stimulating immunoglobulin and acetylcholine receptor antibodies, and electrophysiological evidence of a postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder. In the absence of clinical or biochemical evidence of primary adrenal insufficiency, the coexistence of autoimmune thyroid disease and MG supported a diagnosis of APS3c on the Neufeld and Blizzard classification. Despite methimazole (15 mg/day) and pyridostigmine (600 mg/day) therapy, and good adherence to treatment, biochemical hyperthyroidism persisted and progressed to thyroid storm. During outpatient follow-up, an intrauterine pregnancy was confirmed. Methimazole was withheld during the first trimester while the patient remained clinically stable despite persistent biochemical hyperthyroidism, and it was resumed thereafter. At the time of writing, the pregnancy remains ongoing under multidisciplinary care involving endocrinology, neurology, internal medicine, and maternal-fetal medicine, with serial maternal monitoring, planned third-trimester antibody reassessment, targeted fetal ultrasonography, perinatal planning, and neonatal surveillance. This case highlights APS3c as an important diagnostic framework for the coexistence of Graves' disease and MG and illustrates how management must be continually reassessed in the setting of thyroid storm and pregnancy. Maternal, fetal, and neonatal outcomes remain pending.

candidates.title: A clinicopathological prediction model for remission after transsphenoidal surgery for acromegaly: A retrospective single-center cohort study.
candidates.abstract: Transsphenoidal surgery (TSS) is the primary treatment of choice in acromegaly. Previous research on predicting remission after TSS was mainly based on clinical and radiological data, lacking histopathological evaluation. Our aim is to produce a clinicopathological prediction model for remission after TSS in acromegaly, enabling clinicians to better inform patients on expected treatment outcomes. This single-center study involved retrospective data collection in a large tertiary referral center in The Netherlands. One hundred patients in whom TSS was performed as primary therapy between January 2000 and July 2019 were included. Uni- and multivariate regression models were used to identify predictors of early biochemical remission according to the consensus criteria, long-term remission (defined as an age- and sex-normalized Insuline growth like factor 1and the absence of postoperative treatment (radiation therapy, repeat surgery, or medical therapy) at last follow-up, irrespective of residual tumor on postoperative magnetic resonance imaging ), and long-term remission without residual tumor (defined by the same biochemical and treatment criteria with the additional absence of residual tumor on postoperative magnetic resonance imaging ). In univariate logistic regression, a larger tumor volume, a larger maximum tumor diameter, a higher modified Knosp classification grade, the presence of cavernous sinus invasion, and a higher random growth hormone at diagnosis were significantly associated with lower remission rates. Tumor subtype and proliferation markers were not. In multivariate logistic regression, a simple model with only maximum tumor diameter as an independent variable predicted best for early biochemical remission (OR 0.85, 95% CI 0.78-0.93, P < .001, sensitivity 78.9%, specificity 71.8%), long-term remission (OR 0.79, 95% CI 0.70-0.88, P < .001, sensitivity 79.5%, specificity 73.7%), and long-term remission without residual tumor (OR 0.75, 95% CI 0.66-0.86, P < .001, sensitivity 79.4%, specificity 78.0%). Maximum tumor diameter was the best predictor, while histopathological characteristics were not predictive for remission after TSS in acromegaly in this cohort.

candidates.title: Transforming Growth Factor Beta/Smad Signaling: A Therapeutic Target of Chinese Herbal Medicine for Kidney Disease.
candidates.abstract: Transforming growth factor beta/Smad signaling has emerged as a promising therapeutic target for kidney disease. Increasing evidence suggests that Chinese herbal medicine (CHM), including single herbs, bioactive compounds, herb pairs, and multi-herb formulas, modulates this signaling network in acute kidney injury, chronic kidney disease, and transitions of acute kidney injury-to-chronic kidney disease and acute kidney injury-on-chronic kidney disease. Frequently studied herbs include Rheum officinale (rhubarb), Wolfiporia cocos (Fu Ling), Scutellaria baicalensis (HuangQin), Salvia miltiorrhiza (Dan Shen), Astragalus membranaceus (Huang Qi), and Coptis chinensis (Huang Lian). Experimental studies suggest that CHM interventions act at multiple regulatory levels, including Smad3 activation, Smad3/Smad7 balance, post-translational modification, and epigenetic regulation, while also interacting with oxidative stress, ferroptosis, inflammatory signaling, microRNA regulation, gut microbiota, and renal-immune cell crosstalk. Overall, CHM shows promise as a multitarget strategy against transforming growth factor beta 1/Smad-driven kidney fibrosis, but further mechanistic and multicenter clinical trials are needed.

candidates.title: VIP-Mediated Syndromes: Contrasting Presentations and Multidisciplinary Management of Two Rare Neuroendocrine Tumors.
candidates.abstract: Vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP)-secreting tumors are rare neuroendocrine neoplasms that cause severe secretory diarrhea and electrolyte abnormalities. We describe 2 atypical cases requiring multidisciplinary care. One patient had a VIP-secreting pheochromocytoma with elevated VIP and metanephrine levels; symptoms improved after adrenalectomy. The second had a metastatic small intestinal neuroendocrine tumor with persistent VIP-mediated diarrhea despite debulking and somatostatin analog therapy, complicated by anal fissures, trans-sphincteric perianal fistula, and neuropathic pelvic pain. These cases highlight morbidity and potential complications associated with extrapancreatic VIP hypersecretion and the value of coordinated multidisciplinary management to improve outcomes and quality of life.

candidates.title: Resolving melanoma heterogeneity at single-cell resolution: implications for target discovery and therapy resistance.
candidates.abstract: Melanoma is characterized by profound intra-tumoural heterogeneity and a complex tumour microenvironment (TME), which are primary drivers of therapy resistance. Conventional bulk sequencing lacks the resolution to capture these cellular nuances. Single-cell technologies, particularly single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial multiomics, have fundamentally advanced our understanding of melanoma by enabling high-resolution characterization of malignant cell states, immune ecosystems and tumour microenvironment interactions. In this review, we summarize recent advances in single-cell multiomics studies of melanoma heterogeneity and therapy resistance, focusing on the identification of drug-tolerant persister states, immune escape mechanisms and resistance-associated cellular transitions. We further discuss how single-cell approaches facilitate target discovery, biomarker development and the rational design of combination therapies. By integrating multiomics profiling, computational modelling and pharmacological validation, these technologies provide a framework for translating cellular-level insights into precision therapeutic strategies. Finally, we highlight current challenges and future opportunities for clinical implementation of single-cell-guided approaches in refractory melanoma.

candidates.title: Utility of the ACTH/cortisol ratio for differentiating pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism.
candidates.abstract: No simple, blood-based biomarker to estimate tumor size in dogs with pituitary-dependent hypercortisolism (PDH) has been evaluated. Determine whether the adrenocorticotropic hormone (ACTH)/cortisol ratio differentiates pituitary microadenomas from macroadenomas in dogs with PDH and correlates with pituitary size. Seventy privately-owned dogs with PDH (microadenomas, n = 30; macroadenomas, n = 40). Retrospective multicenter observational study. Endogenous ACTH and cortisol concentrations obtained at the same time point before treatment were used to calculate the ACTH/cortisol ratio. Pituitary tumor size was classified using the pituitary-to-brain (P/B) ratio. Diagnostic performance was evaluated using receiver operating characteristic analysis and multivariable logistic regression. Dogs with macroadenomas had significantly higher ACTH/cortisol ratios than dogs with microadenomas (median, 9.12; IQR, 6.46-14.28 vs median, 4.90; IQR, 3.08-8.10; P < .001). The ratio showed moderate discrimination for differentiating macroadenomas from microadenomas with an area under the curve of 0.77 (95% CI, 0.66-0.89; P < .001). A cutoff >5.69 yielded 85% sensitivity and 60% specificity (positive likelihood ratio 2.13), whereas a higher ratio >11.74 achieved 90% specificity and 35% sensitivity (positive likelihood ratio 3.50). The ACTH/cortisol ratio showed moderate positive correlation with pituitary size (Spearman's ρ = 0.48; 95% CI, 0.26-0.64; P < .001) and remained independently associated with macroadenoma classification in multivariable analysis (OR, 1.19; 95% CI, 1.05-1.40). The ACTH/cortisol ratio is associated with pituitary tumor size in dogs with PDH and may support clinical risk stratification, particularly when advanced imaging is unavailable.

candidates.title: Adrenal ganglioneuroma in an adolescent presenting as an incidentaloma: Imaging-pathology correlation and diagnostic challenges: A case report.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal ganglioneuroma (AGN) is a rare, benign, and usually nonfunctioning tumor arising from neural crest-derived sympathetic ganglion cells. Preoperative diagnosis is difficult because the clinical presentation is often nonspecific, and imaging findings overlap with those of other adrenal neoplasms. We describe an adolescent adrenal incidentaloma with detailed imaging-pathology correlation, adding to the small number of reported adolescent cases. A previously healthy 16-year-old male underwent contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) after a bicycle accident. No traumatic injury was identified, but imaging incidentally revealed a well-circumscribed right adrenal mass measuring approximately 6.1 cm × 3.6 cm × 5.0 cm. CT and magnetic resonance imaging showed progressive, persistent enhancement across the arterial, venous, and delayed phases without demonstrable washout (attenuation increased from 20 Hounsfield units unenhanced to 55 Hounsfield units in the venous phase, with further qualitative enhancement on 15-minute delayed images) and no intralesional fat, suggesting a non-adenomatous lesion and raising suspicion for a neurogenic tumor. Biochemical evaluation showed no evidence of hormonal hypersecretion. Histopathological examination after resection established the diagnosis of AGN. The patient underwent right adrenalectomy because of the size and radiologically indeterminate nature of the mass. The postoperative course was uneventful. Transient elevation of blood pressure noted during follow-up prompted biochemical reevaluation, which showed no evidence of excess catecholamine. Follow-up CT at 9 months showed no recurrence. Progressive delayed enhancement without washout and absence of signal loss on opposed-phase magnetic resonance imaging, a pattern previously described in ganglioneuroma, may suggest the diagnosis preoperatively, although definitive diagnosis requires histopathological confirmation. Complete surgical excision established the diagnosis and achieved a favorable short-term outcome; the excellent long-term prognosis of AGN is supported by the published literature, and our patient remains recurrence-free at 9 months.

candidates.title: Triptonide alleviates sepsis-associated acute lung injury by suppressing the STAT3/HIF-1α-mediated aerobic glycolysis in macrophages.
candidates.abstract: Sepsis-associated acute lung injury (SA-ALI), represents a major contributor to mortality among septic patients during the early hyperinflammatory phase. Triptonide, a diterpenoids extract from Tripterygium wilfordii Hook f has anticancer and contraceptive effects. However, its potential and mechanism in SA-ALI are largely unknown. This study aims to evaluate the therapeutic efficacy and elucidate underlying mechanisms of triptonide in SA-ALI to identify new clinical strategies. Lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-induced endotoxemia model or caecal ligation and puncture (CLP) model was used to induce SA-ALI in mice, accompanied by treatment with triptonide, triptolide and 2-methoxyestradiol. Parallel in vitro experiments involved LPS-treated mouse primary macrophages cultured with or without triptonide. Transcriptomic sequencing of macrophages was performed to explore the anti-inflammatory mechanisms of triptonide, which were further substantiated using specific activators, inhibitors and adeno-associated virus (AAV)-mediated gene targeting. Our data shows that triptonide effectively inhibits macrophage pro-inflammatory activation, reduces pulmonary inflammation and alleviates SA-ALI pathology (i.e. inflammatory cell infiltration, oedema and cell apoptosis), thereby improving the survival of septic mice. Transcriptomic sequencing combined with metabolic analysis shows that triptonide suppresses aerobic glycolysis in pro-inflammatory macrophages by inhibiting the Signal Transducer and Activator of Transcription 3 (STAT3)/Hypoxia inducible factor-1α (HIF-1α) axis. Notably, the therapeutic efficacy of triptonide against SA-ALI was abolished in myeloid cell-specific HIF-1α overexpressed mice (LyzM-CreDIO-hif1a mice). Triptonide protects against SA-ALI by suppressing the STAT3/HIF-1α signalling axis, thereby inhibiting aerobic glycolysis-mediated pro-inflammatory macrophage activation, which suggests that triptonide is a promising therapeutic strategy for SA-ALI.

candidates.title: The Primary Reasons People Participate in Maternal-Fetal Phase I Clinical Trials Are Psychosocial.
candidates.abstract: Recent critiques of ethical guidance for maternal-fetal therapy clinical trials has highlighted the need to weigh maternal, fetal, and societal interests, respectively, while deprioritizing psychosocial reasons for participation. Psychosocial reasons refer to the psychological and social influences on study participants' decisions, and they are often central to considerations about informed consent. However, psychosocial reasons are described as too indirect, subjective, and vague to incorporate into prenatal clinical and regulatory frameworks. This qualitative study examined the perspectives of 11 individuals (within eight couples) enrolled in one of two maternal-fetal therapy phase I clinical trials for rare genetic conditions. Interviews revealed that motivations to participate were primarily psychosocial, including existential concerns given prior bereavement and/or fear of loss; temporal control through taking action as opposed to feeling passive; hope and optimism; and intergenerational and social motivations given one's family experience with disease and desire for social connections. Psychosocial reasons for participating ought to be given more consideration in ethical frameworks for maternal-fetal therapy phase I clinical trials, as well as in the approach to informed consent. It is important for clinical research teams to be especially conscientious to ensure appreciation for participants' reasons for participating that extend beyond typical frameworks of clinical risk/benefit, and to support participants who might harbor optimistic expectations of medical procedures as they transition to postnatal realities.

candidates.title: When genetics disrupt the gut: Dysmotility and ganglioneuromatosis in multiple endocrine neoplasia type 2B syndrome.
candidates.abstract: Multiple Endocrine Neoplasia type 2B (MEN2B) is a rare hereditary cancer syndrome characterized by medullary thyroid carcinoma, mucosal neuromas, and pheochromocytoma. Gastrointestinal involvement is common and often manifests as diffuse intestinal ganglioneuromatosis (IGN), which can impair motility and lead to severe constipation, pseudo-obstruction, or megacolon. We report a male infant with known MEN2B who developed progressive abdominal distension and obstructive symptoms refractory to medical management. Initial rectal suction biopsies were unrevealing. Due to persistent symptoms, a diverting ileostomy was created for decompression, during which full-thickness biopsies were obtained, ultimately establishing the definitive diagnosis of colonic ganglioneuromatosis. This case highlights the limitations of mucosal biopsies in detecting deeper neural pathology and underscores the importance of maintaining clinical suspicion for IGN in patients with MEN2B and persistent gastrointestinal symptoms despite a normal initial evaluation.

candidates.title: Non-diabetic endocrine neuropathies: A practical approach to diagnosis and clinical evaluation.
candidates.abstract: Peripheral neuropathy has diverse etiologies, with endocrine disorders beyond diabetes representing significant, yet frequently underrecognized causes. While diabetic neuropathy is well established, this article specifically excludes a detailed discussion of diabetic neuropathy to focus on less-recognized endocrine causes and presents a practical diagnostic algorithm for their earlier and more accurate identification. A focused narrative review was conducted using PubMed, Scopus and ScienceDirect (2015-2025). From 2,318 screened records, 154 studies were included after full-text review of 298 articles. Evidence was synthesized by etiology, mechanism, clinical presentation and diagnostic relevance. Disorders such as hypothyroidism, acromegaly, adrenal dysfunction and deficiencies of vitamins B12 and D produce distinct neuropathic profiles via metabolic, hormonal, inflammatory or compressive mechanisms. Subclinical nerve involvement is common, with electrophysiological abnormalities detectable in up to 60% of asymptomatic individuals. Characteristic clinical patterns - such as delayed reflexes in hypothyroidism, bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome (CTS) in acromegaly and sensory ataxia in B12 deficiency - provide diagnostic clues. Based on synthesized evidence, a stepwise diagnostic algorithm was developed to guide clinical evaluation. Endocrine disorders are important and often reversible causes of peripheral neuropathy. Early recognition requires a systematic approach. The proposed evidence-based algorithm offers clinicians a practical tool to improve diagnostic efficiency, facilitate timely treatment of the underlying endocrine condition and reduce the risk of irreversible nerve damage.

candidates.title: Radiotherapy for Cervical Cancer: Technical Advances, Clinical Applications, and Future Perspectives.
candidates.abstract: Radiotherapy is an essential treatment modality for cervical cancer and has evolved substantially with advances in image guidance and treatment delivery. This review summarizes recent technological developments in external beam radiotherapy and brachytherapy, their clinical applications, and future directions, with particular consideration of Japanese practice in an international context. In external beam radiotherapy, conventional techniques incorporating central shielding are increasingly being replaced by intensity-modulated radiotherapy (IMRT) and volumetric-modulated arc therapy (VMAT). Daily three-dimensional image-guided radiotherapy (3D-IGRT) is essential for the safe implementation of these techniques because of substantial uterine motion and deformation. In brachytherapy, the transition from two-dimensional point-based prescription to three-dimensional image-guided treatment has enabled individualized assessment of target coverage and doses to organs at risk. Although magnetic resonance imaging-based brachytherapy is internationally recommended, computed tomography-based planning predominates in Japan and has achieved favorable outcomes, despite some studies reporting lower cumulative target doses than those recommended internationally. Intracavitary/interstitial brachytherapy (IC/IS BT) further improves dose distribution by combining intracavitary applicators with interstitial needles, particularly when adequate target coverage cannot be achieved with standard intracavitary brachytherapy alone. Future advances may include artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted treatment planning and adaptive workflows, tissue spacers to overcome anatomical constraints, and the incorporation of genomic, multi-omics, and radiomics information. Integrating these approaches may enable cervical cancer radiotherapy to progress beyond increasingly safe and precise treatment toward personalized care tailored to individual patient and tumor characteristics.
candidates.journal: The journal of obstetrics and gynaecology research

candidates.title: Retinal Microvascular and Peripapillary Profiles in Mild Autonomous Cortisol Secretion Versus Nonfunctioning Adrenal Adenomas.
candidates.abstract: Background/Objectives: Mild autonomous cortisol secretion (MACS) is associated with increased cardiometabolic morbidity, but its relationship with the retinal microcirculation is unknown. We compared retinal and peripapillary microvascular parameters between MACS and nonfunctioning adrenal adenoma (NFA) and, secondarily, examined their associations with continuously modeled post-dexamethasone cortisol. Methods: In this single-center, retrospective, cross-sectional study, 98 patients (45 NFA, 53 MACS) were included, and optical coherence tomography angiography (OCTA) and structural OCT data from one eye per patient were analyzed. The primary outcome was whole-image deep capillary plexus (DCP) vessel density. Multivariable models were adjusted for age, sex, body mass index, and cardiometabolic comorbidities; secondary analyses were corrected using the Benjamini-Hochberg false discovery rate (q values). Results: OCTA was evaluable in 89 patients. The primary outcome did not differ significantly between groups in the main analysis (NFA vs. MACS, 48.64 ± 5.71% vs. 47.31 ± 5.77%; adjusted difference -1.29 percentage points, 95% CI -3.97 to 1.38; p = 0.339) or in any sensitivity analysis. In secondary analyses, superior retinal nerve fiber layer (RNFL) thickness was greater in MACS (β = 17.38 µm; q < 0.001) and increased with ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) (β = 13.74 µm; q = 0.010). Higher ln(post-dexamethasone cortisol) was also associated with lower parafoveal DCP (β = -2.72 percentage points; p = 0.013) and inside-disc radial peripapillary capillary vessel density (β = -3.13 percentage points; p = 0.026), which did not survive multiplicity correction; no superficial capillary plexus sector was associated with either exposure (all p ≥ 0.37). Conclusions: MACS was not significantly associated with whole-image DCP vessel density. The secondary associations with continuous cortisol are cross-sectional and hypothesis-generating and require prospective confirmation.

candidates.title: Acute Sheehan Syndrome Presenting as Panhypopituitarism and Reversible Cardiac Dysfunction in a Patient With Sickle Cell Disease: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Sheehan syndrome is an uncommon cause of hypopituitarism resulting from ischemic pituitary necrosis following severe postpartum hemorrhage (PPH) and hypotension. Its presentation can be delayed and non-specific, and it is rarely reported in the context of mild PPH with severe hemolysis. Here, we describe a 31-year-old woman with underlying sickle cell disease (SCD) who developed panhypopituitarism and reversible cardiac dysfunction after an 11-week period of progressive symptoms following spontaneous vaginal delivery complicated by an estimated blood loss of 700 mL and severe hemolysis. Pituitary hormonal replacement therapy, together with heart failure treatment, resulted in marked clinical and biochemical improvement, with normalization of metabolic abnormalities and recovery of cardiac function. This case suggests a possible association between Sheehan syndrome and postpartum blood loss of 700 mL accompanied by severe hemolysis, though this remains hypothetical based on a single case.

candidates.title: Addison's Disease Mimicking Cerebral Salt Wasting Syndrome: A Case of Severe Hyponatremia.
candidates.abstract: Hyponatremia is a common electrolyte abnormality with varying degrees of severity. It can be asymptomatic if mild and can cause convulsions and coma if severe. Systematic investigation of hyponatremia helps to find out the etiology and proper management. Here, we are presenting the case of a 67-year-old man who presented with vomiting, hyperpigmentation, and hypovolemic hyponatremia due to Addison's disease. Evaluation of hyponatremia showed elevated urinary sodium as expected in Addison's disease, but there was hypouricemia with increased fractional excretion of uric acid suggestive of cerebral salt wasting syndrome. Even with the correct diagnosis, wrong medication interval can cause inadequate rise in serum sodium. Mild thyroid-stimulating hormone elevation can occur in untreated isolated Addison's disease. Addison's disease should always be considered in unexplained hyponatremia even if laboratory findings are suggestive of cerebral salt wasting syndrome. Hyponatremia in Addison's disease may respond poorly to hypertonic saline until glucocorticoid deficiency is corrected, and steroid and fluid replacement is essential and lifesaving.

candidates.title: Scleroderma-Like Phenotype in a Patient With Transthyretin Cardiac Amyloidosis and Acromegaly: A Triple Diagnostic Challenge.
candidates.abstract: Systemic sclerosis, transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis, and acromegaly are rare disorders that share several clinical manifestations, including skin thickening, heart failure, dysphagia, fatigue, and soft tissue enlargement. Their coexistence is exceptionally rare and poses a significant diagnostic challenge, increasing the risk of premature diagnostic closure. We report a 78-year-old man who developed progressive diffuse skin thickening following spinal cord stimulator revision. Positive RNA polymerase III antibodies supported a diagnosis of diffuse systemic sclerosis. Evaluation of worsening edema and exertional dyspnea revealed severe concentric left ventricular hypertrophy with relative apical sparing on echocardiography, and technetium-99m pyrophosphate scintigraphy confirmed transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis. Persistent macroglossia, coarse facial features, prior carpal tunnel syndrome, and a remote history of increasing ring and shoe size prompted endocrine evaluation, which demonstrated elevated insulin-like growth factor-1 levels, failure of growth hormone suppression, and a pituitary macroadenoma consistent with acromegaly. The patient underwent successful transsphenoidal resection with biochemical remission. This case highlights the importance of reconsidering the differential diagnosis when clinical features are not fully explained by an established diagnosis. Recognizing atypical and discordant findings prevented premature diagnostic closure and led to the identification of transthyretin cardiac amyloidosis and acromegaly in a patient with a rapidly progressive scleroderma-like phenotype.

candidates.title: Case Report: Neurosurgery, octreotide, cabergoline, radiotherapy, pasireotide and pegvisomant - a multimodal strategy for adolescent acrogigantism.
candidates.abstract: Growth hormone (GH)-secreting pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs) are rare in the pediatric population. They often present as large, invasive tumors and are frequently associated with an underlying genetic predisposition, making their management particularly challenging. Optimal treatment requires an individualized multidisciplinary approach, which often involves a combination of surgery and adjuvant medical therapy or radiotherapy when necessary. We present a challenging case of an adolescent female with acrogigantism. The patient was diagnosed at the age of 13 years and 10 months during the evaluation of chronic headaches. Brain magnetic resonance imaging revealed an invasive PitNET measuring 38 × 23 × 32 mm, while biochemical assessment confirmed marked GH hypersecretion. The disease followed an aggressive course, and biochemical control could not be achieved despite optimal multimodal therapy. Sequential treatment included neurosurgical resection, octreotide LAR, cabergoline, pasireotide LAR, proton beam radiotherapy, and pegvisomant. Combination therapy with pegvisomant and octreotide LAR ultimately normalized insulin-like growth factor 1 concentrations while maintaining long-term radiological tumor stability. This case underscores the complexity of managing aggressive GH-secreting PitNETs in adolescents and emphasizes the need for individualized, multidisciplinary care and long-term follow-up. Combined medical therapy with pegvisomant and octreotide LAR may provide effective biochemical control when surgery, radiotherapy, and standard medical treatment are insufficient.

candidates.title: Pituitary Apoplexy Complicated by Pulmonary Embolism in a Neurologically Complex Patient: A Diagnostic Challenge.
candidates.abstract: Pituitary apoplexy is a rare endocrine emergency resulting from either acute haemorrhage or infarction within the pituitary gland. Although apoplexy occurs most frequently in a pre-existing pituitary adenoma, apoplexy could be the first presentation of a previously unknown adenoma. Acute headaches, visual disturbances, and neurological symptoms are common presenting symptoms in apoplexy; however, these symptoms may overlap with other neurological emergencies, which necessitate a holistic approach of clinical, radiological, and hormonal evaluation for suspected cases of apoplexy to confirm the diagnosis. Here we present a diagnostically challenging case of a 66-year-old man who presented with a sudden severe headache. His background history included a presumed intraventricular neurocytoma under surveillance. Initial CT head scan suggested possible haemorrhage within a known intraventricular mass (neurocytoma) with no obvious changes within the pituitary gland. However, subsequent MRI head demonstrated radiological features consistent with pituitary apoplexy. Later in his admission, he exhibited bilateral peripheral visual field constriction and early papilledema on fundoscopy. Hormonal testing showed evidence of hypopituitarism. The patient was managed conservatively with intravenous hydrocortisone replacement. During admission, he developed bilateral pulmonary emboli, for which he was treated with anticoagulation. While he was on anticoagulation, he developed intracranial haemorrhage, which led to his death after discharge from the hospital. This case demonstrates the importance of considering pituitary apoplexy in a challenging radiological and clinical presentation. A pre-existing neurological lesion (neurocytoma) makes a holistic approach, including MRI imaging and early hormonal evaluation are essential for timely diagnosis and treatment of pituitary apoplexy. The clinical challenge of having concurrent haemorrhagic and thrombotic events necessitates an individualised approach after balancing the benefits and risks of using anticoagulation treatment.

candidates.title: Solitary Neurofibroma in the Submental Region of a 15-Year-Old Adolescent: A Case Report and Review of Literature.
candidates.abstract: Neurofibroma is a benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor composed of Schwann cells and fibroblasts. It may occur sporadically or as part of neurofibromatosis type 1 (NF1). Solitary neurofibroma arising in the submental region of an adolescent is extremely rare. We report a case of a solitary submental neurofibroma in a 15-year-old male and highlight its diagnostic and management implications. A 15-year-old adolescent boy presented with a chronic, painless right submental swelling that had been present for one year and had enlarged over the preceding three months. Clinical examination revealed a rubbery, nontender, approximately 3×3×4 cm mass without skin changes or systemic symptoms. There was no personal or family history suggestive of NF1, neural tumors, or pheochromocytoma. Ultrasound and CT imaging showed a well-defined soft-tissue mass consistent with a benign neurogenic tumor. The mass was completely excised via a submental incision. Histopathological examination confirmed a solitary neurofibroma with Schwann cell and fibroblast proliferation within a collagen matrix, Antoni A and B patterns, and positive S-100 immunostaining, with no evidence of malignancy. The postoperative course was uneventful, and tongue and floor-of-mouth function were preserved. Solitary submental neurofibroma should be considered in the differential diagnosis of submental masses in adolescents, even in the absence of NF1 features. Complete surgical excision is the treatment of choice and allows definitive histopathological diagnosis. A thorough evaluation for NF1 is recommended to guide long-term management and follow-up.

candidates.title: Durable Complete Response to Pembrolizumab for Postoperative Nodal Recurrence of Lynch Syndrome-Associated Upper Tract Urothelial Carcinoma: A Case Report.
candidates.abstract: Germline mutations in mismatch repair genes cause Lynch syndrome and are associated with upper tract urothelial carcinoma (UTUC). Tumors with deficient mismatch repair (dMMR) or microsatellite instability-high (MSI-H) may respond favorably to immune checkpoint inhibitors. A 54-year-old woman with Lynch syndrome and a germline MSH2 mutation developed right renal pelvic carcinoma. The tumor was diagnosed as a pT3 high-grade urothelial carcinoma, and the patient underwent laparoscopic nephroureterectomy. She was subsequently administered adjuvant gemcitabine and carboplatin due to a contraindication for cisplatin. Due to nodal recurrence, pembrolizumab was initiated at 200 mg every 3 weeks, achieving a complete radiological and metabolic response after five cycles. The course was complicated by immune-related adrenal insufficiency, which was managed with corticosteroid replacement therapy. Pembrolizumab may achieve a durable complete response in Lynch syndrome-associated UTUC. MSI screening should be considered in UTUC to guide decision-making.

candidates.title: Histopathological predictors of extranodal extension in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma: a five-year retrospective cohort study.
candidates.abstract: The extranodal extension (ENE) of cervical nodal metastases is a major adverse prognostic feature in oral cavity squamous cell carcinoma (OCSCC). Despite this clinical significance, the primary histopathological features of the tumour that independently predict ENE as distinct from nodal metastasis remain poorly characterised. This study was undertaken with the aim of addressing that gap. A retrospective cohort of 181 randomly selected patients with OCSCC was analysed from a 5-year institutional database (January 2019-February 2025). Three multivariate logistic regression models were constructed: 1) ENE-positive versus all other cases (global model); 2) Node-positive versus node-negative; and (3) ENE-positive versus node-positive (ENE-negative). Histopathological variables included tumour differentiation, lymphovascular invasion (LVI), perineural invasion (PNI), pattern of invasion, bone involvement, depth of invasion (DOI) and maximum tumour diameter (size). Poor differentiation was the only independent predictor of ENE across all three models (OR 3.67, 95% CI 1.77-7.62, p < 0.001 in the global model; OR 2.58, 95% CI 1.15-5.78, p = 0.021 in node-positive patients). Bone involvement was independently associated with ENE in the global model (OR 7.86, 95% CI 1.33-46.49, p = 0.023). DOI, size, PNI, LVI, and pattern of invasion did not independently predict ENE in any model. The tumour subsite influenced the pattern of invasion and LVI but not ENE or nodal status. ENE in OCSCC appears to be governed by the tumour biology, principally histological grade, rather than by tumour dimensions. Preoperative biopsy grading could carry weight in the stratification of risk and requirement for adjuvant therapy planning.
candidates.journal: The British journal of oral & maxillofacial surgery

candidates.title: Transfemoral transcaval adrenal biopsy: a technical report and review of adrenal biopsy approaches.
candidates.abstract: Despite advances in cross-sectional imaging, adrenal biopsy plays a role in a small subset of lesions that remain indeterminate after complete imaging work-up or in which tissue diagnosis would alter management. Anatomic constraints around the adrenal glands can make safe percutaneous access technically challenging. This technical report describes a transfemoral transcaval approach to biopsy of a right adrenal mass directly abutting the inferior vena cava (IVC) that was not safely accessible by conventional percutaneous routes. Additionally, a concise review of contemporary adrenal biopsy indications and access routes is performed. Adapted from transfemoral transcaval liver biopsy, the technique uses right common femoral venous access, positioning of a reshaped metal guide cannula within the IVC at the level of the lesion adjacent to the right renal vein, and deployment of a core biopsy needle across the caval wall under combined fluoroscopic and ultrasound guidance, with cone-beam CT confirmation of needle position and completion venography to exclude caval injury. Diagnostic tissue was obtained without periprocedural complication; histopathology demonstrated an unexpected pheochromocytoma, a finding discussed here in detail due to its implications for pre-procedure biochemical evaluation. This limited experience demonstrates technical feasibility in carefully selected patients. The safety and comparative effectiveness of the technique require evaluation in larger series.

candidates.title: From Lethargy to Recovery: Central Diabetes Insipidus from Pituitary Metastasis in Recurrent HER2-Positive Breast Cancer Treated with Fam-Trastuzumab Deruxtecan-Nxki.
candidates.abstract: HER2-positive breast cancer is well known for its aggressive nature and high incidence of central nervous system (CNS) metastasis, often affecting the brain parenchyma or leptomeninges. However, metastasis to the pituitary gland is exceedingly rare. We report a case of ER/PR-negative, HER2-positive breast cancer recurrence presenting with panhypopituitarism (PH) and central diabetes insipidus (CDI), resulting in hypernatremia-induced altered mental status. The patient had completed prior treatment with neoadjuvant chemotherapy, lumpectomy, and trastuzumab. Imaging revealed a temporal lobe mass with suprasellar enhancement. Surgical resection confirmed breast carcinoma metastasis. Hormonal studies confirmed PH and CDI. Management involved DDAVP, corticosteroids, fluid correction, whole-brain radiation, and systemic therapy with fam-trastuzumab deruxtecan-nxki (ENHERTU), leading to significant neurological recovery. This case highlights a rare metastatic pattern and the need for high clinical suspicion and multidisciplinary intervention.

candidates.title: Immune checkpoint inhibitor-induced multi-organ immune damage complicated by severe pneumonia: case report.
candidates.abstract: Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) have substantially extended survival in patients with extensive-stage small-cell lung cancer (ES-SCLC), yet they also carry the risk of life-threatening immune-related adverse events (irAEs). Clinical experience in managing multi-organ irAEs (MO-irAEs) complicated by respiratory failure and subsequent severe pneumonia remains exceedingly scarce. Here we report a 71-year-old patient with ES-SCLC (stage IVb, with brain and splenic metastases) who, after four cycles of serplulimab plus chemotherapy, sequentially developed myocarditis, myositis, and hepatic injury. Following premature tapering of glucocorticoid therapy, the patient experienced a recurrence of ICI-related toxicity, manifesting as hypophysitis, primary hypothyroidism, and adrenal insufficiency-alongside respiratory failure-and later acquired multidrug-resistant infection during the treatment course. Through individualized moderate-dose glucocorticoids, comprehensive hormone replacement, and pathogen-directed antimicrobial therapy with eravacycline and ceftazidime-avibactam guided by metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS), the infection was ultimately brought under control and multi-organ dysfunction reversed. This case underscores several key points: (1) serplulimab can precipitate multi-endocrine gland insufficiency, and severe hypothyroidism may be one of the factors contributing to the respiratory failure, mandating a high index of clinical suspicion; (2) glucocorticoid regimens should adhere to adequate initial dosing, sufficient duration, and slow tapering-abrupt discontinuation risks triggering recurrence of ICI-related toxicity; and (3) rapid, precise lower-respiratory-tract pathogen identification coupled with targeted antimicrobial therapy offers particular value in managing severe pneumonia caused by drug-resistant organisms.

candidates.title: Characterizing bone metastases and skeletal-related events in patients with well-differentiated neuroendocrine neoplasms utilizing 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography.
candidates.abstract: Tumors of neuroendocrine origin are a heterogenous group of related neoplasms which can arise from anywhere in the body. Neuroendocrine neoplasms (NENs) are categorized by site of origin, differentiation status and grade (Ki-67 expression and/or mitotic rate), with significant prognostic variability accordingly. Historically, the prevalence of bone metastasis is reported to be 6%-12% based on "first generation" (i.e., 111Indium pentetreotide [Octreoscan®]) somatostatin receptor imaging (SSRI). We conducted a retrospective cohort study including patients with well-differentiated NENs to determine the clinical and imaging characteristics of osseous metastases when evaluated with higher-sensitivity 68Gallium-DOTATATE positron emission tomography (PET) scans, as well as determining fracture prevalence in selected sub-cohorts. We also developed a risk score analysis to assess risk of fracture in this cohort. Four hundred twenty-four patients were identified for inclusion. The median age was 61 years. Most patients were asymptomatic (64%), had sclerotic lesions (77%), Krenning 4 (71%), and had >3 sites (69%) of osseous disease. A high proportion of patients had osseous metastases at sites with high risk for fracture, including vertebra (82%), pelvis (63%), and peri-trochanteric femur (34%). Fifty-seven patients (13%) in the entire cohort suffered a fracture. Fracture prevalence was significantly lower in small bowel neuroendocrine tumors (NETs, 7%) and Grades 1 and 2 disease (8% and 9%, respectively), with higher prevalence in pancreatic NETs, paragangliomas/pheochromocytomas, lung carcinoid, and Grade 3 disease (≥20% for each; p-values <.05). Our study showed that the rate of osseous metastatic disease approximates 20% in well-differentiated NENs. Most bone metastases are asymptomatic and the risk of fracture is variable based on the primary site of disease and tumor grade. Our novel risk score analysis for fracture was designed to assist clinician decision making as to management of bone metastasis in this patient population.

candidates.title: A Diagnostic Conundrum: A Hemorrhagic Adrenal Mass With Discordant Radiological, Biochemical, and Pathologic Features.
candidates.abstract: Adrenal incidentalomas vary in their identity, making accurate diagnosis essential for management. Interpretation of these lesions using radiology, biochemistry, or pathology can be confounded by hemorrhagic changes, medication effects, and limitations of imaging. To prevent misclassification, an integrated assessment is crucial. We present a case of a 71-year-old male with an incidentally discovered left adrenal mass that exhibited computed tomography and MRI imaging findings concerning for pheochromocytoma or adrenal malignancy. Biochemical analysis ruled out pheochromocytoma and was suggestive of possible glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid co-secretion, although clinical urgency of surgical resection precluded completion of confirmatory endocrinologic testing. The lesion was initially diagnosed as a benign endothelial adrenal cyst on pathologic review. Because of the discordance among the radiological, biochemical, and initial pathologic findings, an integrated histologic re-evaluation was requested. The mass was ultimately reclassified as an adrenocortical adenoma with extensive hemorrhagic and cystic changes. This case highlights the importance of multidisciplinary integration when evaluating adrenal lesions with confounding features and underscores how suggestive (though incomplete) biochemical evidence can appropriately drive pathological re-evaluation.

candidates.title: Lecanemab in Singapore: Appropriate use recommendations for early Alzheimer's disease.
candidates.abstract: Lecanemab, a monoclonal antibody targeting β-amyloid oligomers, protofibrils, and insoluble fibrils, has been approved for Alzheimer's disease (AD) treatment in Singapore, based on the phase 3 Clarity AD study. In this paper, the Singapore-adapted Appropriate Use Recommendations (AURs) serve to assist Singapore physicians in identifying patients who will likely benefit from treatment while ensuring effective monitoring. The AURs are based on the Singaporeapproved prescribing information combined with lecanemab phase 2 and 3 clinical trials and real-world data up to April 2026. The decision to initiate lecanemab should be based on careful evaluation of individuals, including Singapore-validated cognitive status tests to identify mild cognitive impairment (MCI) due to AD and mild AD dementia. Other important evaluations include baseline brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), assessment of the apolipoprotein E ε4 (APOEε4) genotype, and amyloid pathology confirmation. Guidance on identifying patients at increased risk of amyloid-related imaging abnormalities (ARIA) during treatment and other patient profiles warranting additional caution is provided. Recommendations for monitoring patients, managing infusion-related reactions, and identifying lecanemab discontinuation scenarios are included. Lecanemab should only be prescribed for patients with MCI due to AD or mild AD dementia following careful clinical evaluation confirming AD pathology, with caution exercised in patients at increased ARIA risk (e.g. APOEε4 gene carriers). During treatment, patients should receive regular monitoring for ARIA symptoms including follow-up MRI scans. Future directions include the development of a Singapore-specific registry to monitor patients and gather long-term data to support a consensus-driven framework to inform and optimise the use of lecanemab in Singapore.
candidates.journal: Annals of the Academy of Medicine, Singapore

candidates.title: Hotspot mutations and tumour spectrum in von Hippel-Lindau syndrome: genotype-phenotype analysis of a large Chinese cohort.
candidates.abstract: Von Hippel-Lindau (VHL) syndrome is a rare autosomal dominant multisystem tumour syndrome caused by germline VHL mutations. The traditional classification of VHL syndrome, which is largely based on pheochromocytoma penetrance, is insufficient for individualised surveillance and management. This study aimed to improve mutation-specific risk stratification and define genotype-phenotype correlations of recurrent hotspot mutations in a large Chinese cohort. This retrospective single-centre study included 674 patients with VHL disease from 283 unrelated families. Four recurrent hotspot mutation subtypes were analysed: codon 65 missense mutations, exon 2 deletion, c.481C > T, and c.224_226del. Kaplan-Meier analysis and univariate and multivariate Cox regression models were used to assess age-related tumour risks and survival outcomes. Codon 65 missense mutations were associated with a lower risk of retinal angioma and pheochromocytoma, indicating a relatively mild phenotype. Exon 2 deletion was characterised by a higher prevalence, earlier onset, and increased age-related risk of retinal angioma and worse renal cell carcinoma (RCC)-specific survival. Increased prevalences and age-related risks of central nervous system hemangioblastoma (CHB), RCC, and pancreatic cysts or tumours were associated with c.481C > T mutations. The c.224_226del subtype showed a distinct CHB-predominant phenotype, with higher CHB incidence, earlier onset, lower pancreatic lesion risk, and higher overall mortality. Recurrent hotspot VHL mutation subtypes were associated with distinct clinical phenotypes and prognostic patterns. Mutation subtype-based classification (covering 19.6% of patients with VHL syndrome) may provide more precise guidance for surveillance, clinical decision-making, and genetic counselling than traditional broad classification models.
